goal: Make the installed `bitcoin` wrapper look for helper binaries in the actual configured install directories instead of hardcoded bin/libexec.
Fixes a real failure on Arch Linux where `bitcoin -m node` and similar commands fail outright because Arch installs binaries into a different libexec-equivalent directory.
reviewability: Ready. All raised concerns (bindir assumption, configure-time checks, test layout, valgrind resolution) were fixed in subsequent pushes and CI is green.

cyb3ralbert independently built and verified the fix resolves the Arch scenario, and found test gaps the author fixed (cyb3ralbert).

result.summary: This PR makes the installed `bitcoin` wrapper honor CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR and CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBEXECDIR instead of hardcoded 'bin'/'libexec' strings when locating sibling executables like bitcoind. It threads the configured directories through bitcoin-build-config.h, adds configure-time and compile-time guards against empty values, and adds a functional test that fakes an installed layout to exercise the lookup path that normal build-tree tests never hit. It supersedes three earlier closed PRs (#36037, #35789, #36085) building toward the same fix.
result.problem: On Arch Linux (and any distro configuring non-default install directories) the installed `bitcoin` wrapper fails with 'execvp failed to execute ... No such file or directory' for commands like `bitcoin -m node` or `bitcoin chainstate`, because the wrapper assumes binaries sit in hardcoded bin/libexec directories rather than the ones actually configured at build time (issue #35785).

open_concerns: cyb3ralbert suggested a CI job be added that builds with a non-default CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBEXECDIR so this regression path stays covered going forward; author agreed but deferred to a followup PR since CI config changes need different review.
resolved_concerns: hebasto's concern about BITCOIN_BINDIR being restricted to a single path component was addressed with an expanded comment and configure-time FATAL_ERROR checks.
hebasto's redundant GNUInstallDirs include was removed.
hebasto's suggestion to use tmpdir directly instead of the node datadir for the fake install prefix was implemented.
cyb3ralbert's report that the new test silently skipped its checks under --valgrind (and later, failed outright) was fixed by resolving valgrind's path before PATH is blanked.

categories.name: build
categories.evidence: Adds GNUInstallDirs include ordering, configure-time FATAL_ERROR guards for empty install dirs, and threads CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR/LIBEXECDIR into bitcoin-build-config.h; core files are CMakeLists.txt and cmake/module files.
categories.rationale: P2 because it fixes real breakage for users on distributions (Arch Linux) that configure non-default install directories, a supported-platform failure category the bands treat seriously. It is narrow in scope, affecting only wrapper lookup logic, not general build/CI reliability, so it does not reach P1.

The open followup about adding CI coverage for non-default libexecdir was explicitly deferred by the author, so it does not count against reviewability, but it means a regression here would currently go undetected by CI.
result.card: This PR fixes a wrapper bug where the installed `bitcoin` command fails outright on distributions like Arch Linux that configure non-default CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR/LIBEXECDIR values, by making the wrapper's sibling-executable lookup use the configured directories instead of hardcoded 'bin'/'libexec' strings. It supersedes three earlier attempts (#36037, #35789, #36085) and adds a functional test exercising the installed-layout lookup path that normal build-tree tests never hit. Two reviewers, hebasto and cyb3ralbert, independently rebuilt the branch and confirmed the fix resolves the reported Arch scenario (#35785), and hebasto gave an Approach ACK; all concerns raised (bindir assumptions, configure-time checks, valgrind path resolution in the new test) were fixed in follow-up pushes. The PR is Ready for review with CI green and no open objections; a suggested CI-coverage improvement was explicitly deferred to a followup. It touches build (CMakeLists.txt/GNUInstallDirs), the `bitcoin` wrapper as a tool, and ipc's explicitly-listed wrapper scope, with the strongest impact in build and tools since the bug directly breaks basic node launching on a real distribution.
